rationale: The outcome-blind Gate 2C audit selects regional forcing at a 95% unit-coverage tolerance, but the selected scale changes to species-wide under a 97.5% or 100% completeness requirement. The primary regional result therefore requires a predeclared species-wide forcing sensitivity.

threshold_audit.selection_rule_at_regional_levels: finest APBP or CCAMLR level with at least two qualifying groups and qualifying-group unit coverage at or above the threshold; otherwise species-wide if supported

mandatory_sensitivity.rule: Refit the same demographic process and the same frozen site-predictor tests with one species-wide shared forcing per species. Do not retune priors, predictors, temporal window, observation model, or site-trait transforms.

interpretation_rule: A response-filter conclusion is scale-robust only if the primary regional-forcing analysis and the species-wide sensitivity agree in the qualitative direction of the focal site-trait effect and do not reverse the A x H crossover.
If the regional and species-wide analyses disagree materially, report the response-filter result as forcing-scale dependent rather than choosing the scale that gives the stronger ecological effect.

The regional forcing analysis remains primary because it was selected by the frozen 95% outcome-blind support rule; the species-wide fit is a mandatory sensitivity, not a competing post-outcome model search.
boundary: No demographic count magnitude, fitted trend, fitted loading, or site-trait association was inspected to define this sensitivity.
The 90/95/97.5/100% threshold audit uses only Gate 2C support metadata.
No additional geographic partition may be introduced after outcomes are opened.
